name: Siena
tagline: Gothic hill town of the Palio and Tuscan hills
summary: Siena is the Gothic jewel of Tuscany, centred on the shell-shaped Piazza del Campo where the Palio horse race runs each summer. Climb the Torre del Mangia, see the striped Duomo and its marble floors, then head out to San Gimignano's towers and the cypress roads of the Val d'Orcia.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are ideal; the Palio on 2 July and 16 August packs the city.
arrival: Buses from Florence take about 75 minutes and stop near the centre; Pisa and Florence airports are the nearest.
gettingAround: The old town is car-free and steep; rent a car or join a tour for the countryside.
cashTip: Cards work almost everywhere; carry a few euros for coffee bars, tips and small shops.
foodTip: Pici pasta, wild boar ragù, panforte and Chianti wines.
buyTip: Panforte, ricciarelli biscuits, contrada flags and ceramics.
baseArea: Inside the walls near Il Campo
